name: Earth, Environmental, and Planetary Sciences
notes: This is the department's current BS, replacing the retired BS in Environmental Science (EVS), which is no longer offered to new students and is deliberately absent from this app.
19 courses total, with a choice of three tracks: Climate and Environmental Sciences, Geosciences, or Earth and Planetary Sciences.

The three tracks differ in how their 19 courses are apportioned (Climate: 4 advanced core + 4 technical electives; Geosciences: 4 advanced core + 3 technical electives; Earth and Planetary: 3 advanced core + 5 technical electives). The app models the advanced core as a track choice and then a shared block of four technical electives drawn from the union of the three track lists - so the exact per-track elective count is approximate. Confirm your track's split with the department.
The Geosciences track additionally requires four one-credit 200-level labs, at least three from EES Department courses. Lab components are marked (L) on the page and are not separately modeled.

Up to two 200-level courses in biology, chemistry, chemical engineering, earth and environmental sciences, or physics may be substituted for a technical elective with advisor approval. Additional advanced core or closure courses may also count as technical electives.
EESC 201, EESC 211, and EESC 223 may substitute for an advanced core course in the Climate track with advisor approval via the course-approval form.
AP credit is acceptable for the supporting science and math courses upon approval.
Possible substitutions for the introductory sequence, with approval: EESC 100, EESC 103, EESC 129, EESC 201.

requirementGroups.label: Chemistry
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Chemistry: CHEM 131: Chemical Concepts, Systems, and Practices I; CHEM 132: Chemical Concepts, Systems, and Practices II

requirementGroups.label: Mathematics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Series one (all three courses are required for this series): MATH 161: Calculus lA; MATH 162: Calculus IIA; MATH 165: Linear Algebra with Differential Equations (or MATH 163). Series two (all four courses are required for this series): MATH 141; MATH 142; MATH 143; MATH 165

requirementGroups.label: Physics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Physics: PHYS 113 or 121: General Physics I / Mechanics; PHYS 114 or 122: General Physics II / Electricity and Magnetism

requirementGroups.label: Introductory sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Both of the following courses: EESC 101: Introduction to Earth Science; EESC 105: Introduction to Climate Change. Possible substitutions with approval: EESC 100, EESC 103, EESC 129, EESC 201

requirementGroups.label: Advanced core courses (track)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must complete one of the following tracks. Track: Climate and Environmental Sciences - Choose four advanced core courses. Track: Geosciences - Choose four of the following advanced core courses. Track: Earth and Planetary Sciences - Choose three of the following advanced core courses.
requirementGroups.note: Modeled at the smallest track requirement (3); the Climate and Geosciences tracks require 4.

requirementGroups.label: Skills course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following skills courses: EESC 214: Earth Science Data Analysis; EESC 251: Intro to Geographic Information Systems; CSC 161: Introduction to Programming; STAT 180: Introduction to Applied Statistical Methodology

requirementGroups.label: Technical electives (4)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose four technical electives (Climate) / Choose three of the following technical electives (Geosciences) / Choose five of the following technical electives (Earth and Planetary). Up to two 200-level courses in biology, chemistry, chemical engineering, earth and environmental sciences, or physics can be substituted for a technical elective with the approval from advisor.
requirementGroups.note: Per-track counts differ (3-5); modeled as four 200-level EESC courses.

requirementGroups.label: Closure course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following closure courses: EESC 299(L): Field Experience; EESC 306: Atmospheric Research; EESC 307: Advanced Seminar on Climate and Environmental Change; EESC 312(W): Research in Ocean Biogeochemistry; EESC 320(W): Sustainable Systems; EESC 368(W): Principles of Experimental Geochemistry; EESC 391(W): Independent Study; EESC 393W(L): Senior Thesis; EESC 394: Internship in Environmental Sciences; EESC 395W: Independent Research
requirementGroups.note: Union of the three tracks' closure lists.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two upper-level writing courses within the major
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Writing Requirement: Two of the courses for the major must be taken as upper-level writing courses, indicated by a 'W' after the course number.
